rationale: The report reproduces on v1: java.net.URI keeps the trailing dot of an absolute DNS name, and the host rules compare exact strings, so localhost. and *.local. pass while resolving to the same loopback or LAN hosts. The rules are private methods inside UrlValidator mixed with parsing; extracting them first makes the fix a one-class change that the full suite can prove behavior-preserving.

impact.reason: isNonPublicHost compares host strings exactly; "localhost." and "*.local." bypass it (the defect)
existing rule tests must keep passing through the refactor and the fix
sole caller of UrlValidator.normalize; behavior for valid URLs must not change
contract unchanged: invalid URLs already map to 400 INVALID_URL

defect.rootCause: exact string comparison on a host that may carry the absolute-name trailing dot

plan: refactor: extract host classification without behavior change
fix: canonicalize the absolute name once, then apply every rule
